subject: Regional handover, egress cadence and subprocessor cadence: initial ask
messages:
From: Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@datastorecorp.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial residency questions for onboarding (EU pinning)

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We need to confirm a few operational commitments before we proceed with the pilot:

1) Residency/pinning: we require that customer-record-level inference for the pilot remains resident in EU region (Frankfurt) for the duration of the trial. Please confirm what your "pinning" guarantee looks like (SLO, enforcement, and exception windows).

2) Transient cross-region processing: we understand some short-lived failover or analytics hops may occur. What is the maximum transient egress window you accept for pinned data? Any telemetry/analytics that temporarily leaves EU must be limited in duration and logged.

3) Subprocessors: please provide a roster (names, roles, region) for any subprocessors that might touch EU-pinned data during routine operations or failover. We will need a security contact for each subprocessor.

4) KMS and encryption: clarify whether keys for the pilot will be customer-managed (BYOK) or Redwood-managed, and whether split-KMS (control plane in US, data plane in EU) is possible.

5) Evidence and timeline: audit log access, retention windows, and a proposed timeline to get the proof artifacts we ask for (SOC2 evidence, sample audit logs, and subprocessor attestations).

We are hoping to start the pilot week of Oct 11; before that we need a short operations playbook and the subprocessor roster. Can you get back to us with a proposed handover checklist and any exceptions you anticipate?

Thanks,

Ava Reynolds
Head of Cloud Security
DataStore Corp
ava.reynolds@datastorecorp.com

--
Attachment: onboarding_requirements_summary.pdf (pdf, 32KB)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@datastorecorp.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Initial residency questions for onboarding (EU pinning)

Hi Ava — thanks for the clear list. Summary responses below and next steps.

Short answers up front:
- We can commit to EU-region pinning for inference payloads with operational constraints (see items below).
- Transient cross-region processing: standard maximum window is 72 hours for emergency failover or burst replication; non-emergency analytics hops are limited to 24 hours unless specified in the DPA addendum. All transient hops are logged and flagged in the audit stream.
- Subprocessors: attached is the current roster (subprocessor_roster_20260929.csv).
- KMS: BYOK is supported for Private/Dedicated customers. For Hosted pilots we can offer a split-KMS arrangement: customer key for data plane (EU) + Redwood-managed control plane key.
- Evidence: we can provide sanitized audit samples, SOC2 cover page, and per-subprocessor attestations on a 10-business-day cadence after signature of an addendum.

Operational ask / proposed handover checklist (short):
1) Sign DPA addendum narrow-scope (we will draft — legal loop).
2) Receive customer's desired pin start date and any blocked IPs.
3) Ops to run a dry run to validate pinning for a representative dataset (2–4 hours).
4) Exchange access: provide read-only audit link + S3 ingress sweep to confirm no egress during run.
5) Go/no-go call 48 hours before start.

Attachments (for your review):
- subprocessor_roster_20260929.csv — names, roles, region, security contact.
- operational-handover-playbook_v1.pdf — high-level steps we will execute for the pilot.
- mateo_residency_matrix_v1.xlsx — mapping table showing which artifacts remain in EU vs. temporary telemetry.

Open questions for your team (please confirm):
- Are you comfortable with the 72-hour emergency window and 24-hour analytics window as described? If not, what windows are acceptable?
- Do you require BYOK for pilot start or is split-KMS acceptable as interim?

I'll loop in Ops/Infra internally to confirm implementation details + a draft DPA addendum.

Best,

— Mateo Alvarez
Head of Product — Platform
Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

Subject: Fwd: Initial residency questions for onboarding (ops/legal action items)

Folks — forwarding DataStore's ask and my reply. High priority pilot; they want the playbook and subprocessor roster this week. Quick notes inline below.

> On Tue, 29 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700 Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@datastorecorp.com> wrote:
> > (external request list)

Internal action items: 
- Laura: please draft a narrow DPA addendum that limits the exception windows and requires audit log visibility. They are likely to ask for higher EU uptime in the doc; let's propose 99.9% residency SLO with an operational fallback matrix (we'll negotiate to 99.95% as escalation). Target: initial draft by Thu EOD (2026-10-01).
- Marcus: confirm the telemetry pipeline: what metrics are logged when we perform a transient hop (fields, retention, redaction rules). Need a short sample of sanitized audit lines by Fri 2026-10-02.
- Olga (Ops): runbook review: can we guarantee the 72h emergency window today? If not, propose recommended lower bound and list tech blockers. Also confirm whether we can generate per-request egress flags for the audit stream (ops trace IDs).

Please include estimated timelines inline and copy Legal when you have a draft. I will coordinate the go/no-go and the pilot dry run once we have the artifacts.

Thanks — Mateo

> Internal-only: Ops must be prepared to run a location-constrained restart for pinned model replicas.

From: Legal - DataCust <legal@datacust.io>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, ava.reynolds@datastorecorp.com
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial residency questions for onboarding (EU pinning)

Hi Mateo / Ava —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. DataStore's legal reviewed the provisional windows and asked us to confirm three items before signature:

1) SLA target: they requested 99.95% residency guarantee for EU-pinned inference. We can accept 99.9% as a contractual baseline for the pilot but will consider 99.95% for committed (paid) Dedicated capacity.
2) IP ranges & egress endpoints: they asked for a list of IP ranges and CDN/egress endpoints that might be used for transient analytics hops. Olga, can you provide an exportable list?
3) DocuSign: please send the DPA addendum via DocuSign (legal@datacust.io to sign).

They also asked for a short sample of sanitized audit logs showing a transient hop event (timestamp, request id, region from->to, reason code). Marcus — can you produce one example by end of day Monday (2026-10-04)?

If we can get the playbook + DPA addendum + sample logs within the timelines above, DataStore expects to sign and schedule the dry run for Oct 12.

Regards,

E. Chen (on behalf of DataCust legal)
